statement: In all TypeScript files, code must compile under TypeScript strict mode (tsconfig strict: true, noImplicitAny).
In all TypeScript files, code should not use the `any` type.

quote: Prefer explicit types for public APIs
statement: In all TypeScript files, public functions and methods should declare explicit parameter and return types.
In all TypeScript files, object shapes should be declared with `type` aliases rather than `interface`.
In all TypeScript files, variant types should be modelled as discriminated unions when appropriate.
In all TypeScript files, fields and properties that are not reassigned should be marked `readonly`.
In all TypeScript files, code should not introduce type parameters that are not needed.

quote: Use dependency injection instead of manual instantiation
statement: In NestJS code under src/**, services and providers must be obtained through NestJS dependency injection, not instantiated manually with `new`.
In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, controllers should be thin and only delegate to services.
In src/**, business logic must live in services (src/features/**/*.service.ts), not in controllers.

quote: Avoid placing business logic inside controllers
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, controllers should not contain business logic.
In src/**, classes should compose dependencies rather than extend base classes, except for true inheritance hierarchies.
In src/**, reusable logic should be packaged as NestJS providers.
In src/api/**/dtos/**, DTO classes should declare every field explicitly and carry validation decorators.

quote: Use class-validator and class-transformer for request validation
statement: In request DTOs, validation must use `class-validator` decorators and `class-transformer` transforms rather than hand-written checks.
In NestJS classes under src/**, dependencies should be injected through the constructor rather than property injection.
In src/**, modules and files should not form circular imports (no `forwardRef` workarounds).

quote: Keep guards, interceptors, and pipes reusable and focused
statement: In src/common/**, guards, interceptors and pipes should each handle one reusable concern.

quote: Prefer explicit return types for services and controllers
statement: In *.service.ts and *.controller.ts, methods should declare explicit return types.
In API code, asynchronous code must use async/await rather than `.then()` chains.
In API code, errors must be handled explicitly.

quote: Use NestJS exception filters when appropriate
statement: In API code, error-to-response translation should go through NestJS exception filters (GlobalExceptionFilter).
In API code, all external input (body, query, params) must be validated, via validated DTOs.

quote: Do not expose internal errors to clients
statement: In API code, internal error details must not be returned to clients.
In src/**, API logic should live in services, not in controllers.

quote: Keep controllers responsible only for transport layer concerns
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, controllers should handle only transport concerns (routing, guards, validation, response mapping).

quote: Prefer RESTful conventions unless project architecture requires otherwise
statement: In src/api/** controllers, routes should follow RESTful conventions.

quote: Keep database access inside dedicated repositories/services
statement: In src/**, database access (PrismaService) should only happen inside dedicated repositories or services.

quote: Avoid direct database access inside controllers
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, controllers should not access PrismaService or the database directly.
In repositories, multi-step database mutations should be wrapped in a Prisma transaction (`$transaction`).
In repositories and services, code should not issue database queries inside loops over results (N+1).
In test files, tests must be deterministic.
In test files, setup logic should not be duplicated across tests.
In test files, test names must describe the behaviour under test.
In unit tests, external dependencies (Prisma, Redis, etc.) should be replaced with mocks.

quote: Negative test cases must go first
statement: In test files, negative test cases must come before positive test cases.

quote: Negative and positive cases must be placed in separate `describe` blocks
statement: In test files, negative and positive cases must be in separate `describe('negative cases')` and `describe('positive cases')` blocks.

quote: Separate describe blocks with an empty line
statement: In test files, sibling `describe` blocks must be separated by an empty line.
Generated code (database-manager/generated/**, *.generated.ts) must never be edited by hand.
In src/**/*.{ts,tsx}, file names must be kebab-case (middle extensions like .service ignored).
In src/**, folder names must be kebab-case.
In TypeScript files, modules must not use default exports; use named exports.
In TypeScript files, tests must not use `.only` (describe.only, it.only).
In TypeScript files, functions must not exceed a cognitive complexity of 20.
In TypeScript files, conditionals must not have all branches identical.
In TypeScript files, nested `if` statements that can be merged must be collapsed.
In TypeScript files, collection size/length checks must not be always-true or always-false (e.g. `length >= 0`).
In TypeScript files, two branches of a conditional or switch must not have the same implementation.
In TypeScript files, collection elements must not be overwritten unconditionally before being used.
In TypeScript files, code must not read from or iterate collections that are always empty.
In TypeScript files, boolean conditions must not be always true or always false.
In TypeScript files, if/else-if chains must not repeat the same condition.
In TypeScript files, binary operators must not have identical operands on both sides.
In TypeScript files, functions must not have identical implementations (duplicate functions).
In TypeScript files, return values of side-effect-free functions must not be ignored.
In TypeScript files, boolean checks must not be inverted with `!(a === b)`; use the opposite operator.
In TypeScript files, boolean literals must not be used redundantly in comparisons or conditions.
In TypeScript files, `switch` statements must have at least three cases; use `if` otherwise.
In TypeScript files, created error objects must be thrown, not discarded.
In TypeScript files, collections that are only written to and never read must not exist.
In TypeScript files, the return value of functions that return nothing must not be used.
In TypeScript files, code must not use non-existent operators such as `=+`, `=-` or `=!`.
In TypeScript files, a value must be returned directly instead of being assigned to a local variable that is immediately returned.
In TypeScript files, `Array.prototype.reduce` calls must pass an initial value.
In TypeScript files, code must not use `@ts-ignore`, `@ts-nocheck` or undescribed `@ts-expect-error` comments.
In TypeScript files, object types must be defined with `type`, not `interface`.
In TypeScript files, type-only imports must use `import type`.
In TypeScript files, functions and methods must declare an explicit return type.
In TypeScript files, type-like names (types, interfaces, enums, type parameters, classes) must be PascalCase.
In TypeScript files, class names must be StrictPascalCase or UPPER_CASE.
In TypeScript files, void-returning expressions must not be used as values, except as arrow-function shorthand bodies.
In TypeScript files, `delete obj[key]` with computed keys is allowed (records used as dictionaries).
In TypeScript files, variables must not shadow variables from an outer scope.
In TypeScript files, there must be no unused variables, and no unused arguments after the last used one; rest siblings are not exempt.
In TypeScript files, explicit `as` casts to non-nullable types are allowed instead of `!` assertions.
In TypeScript files, `??` must be used instead of `||` for nullish defaults, except for string operands.
In TypeScript files, private class members that are never reassigned must be marked `readonly`.
In TypeScript files, template literal expressions must be strings or numbers only.
In TypeScript files, `return await` style is not enforced either way.
In TypeScript files, `switch` statements over union or enum types must handle every member.
In TypeScript files, built-in errors must be created with a message argument.
In TypeScript files, `await` must not be used on elements passed to Promise.all/allSettled/any/race.
In TypeScript files, `instanceof` must not be used with built-in types like Array or String; use Array.isArray or typeof.
In TypeScript files, Promise.all/any/race must not be called with a single-element array.
In TypeScript files, objects and classes must not define a `then` property.
In TypeScript files, async functions must not wrap returns in Promise.resolve or Promise.reject.
In TypeScript files, spreads that only copy a literal or iterable unnecessarily must not be used.
In TypeScript files, useless `undefined` (e.g. `return undefined`, `let x = undefined`) must not be written, except as call arguments and arrow bodies.
In TypeScript files, arrays must be flattened with `Array#flat()` rather than reduce/concat idioms.
In TypeScript files, modern DOM APIs (before/after/replaceWith) must be used instead of insertBefore/replaceChild.
In TypeScript files, Node built-in modules must be imported with the `node:` protocol (e.g. `node:fs`).
In TypeScript files, `Number.isNaN`, `Number.parseInt` etc. must be used instead of the global equivalents.
In TypeScript files, `startsWith`/`endsWith` must be used instead of regex anchors for prefix/suffix checks.
In TypeScript files, deep copies must use `structuredClone` instead of JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...)).
In TypeScript files, type-check failures must throw `TypeError` rather than `Error`.
In TypeScript files, errors must be thrown with `new` (throw new Error(...)).
In TypeScript files, array method callbacks (map, filter, reduce...) must return a value; implicit `return;` is allowed.
In TypeScript files, identifiers including object property names must be camelCase.
In TypeScript files, class methods that do not use `this` are allowed.
In TypeScript files, comparisons must use `===`/`!==`, except `== null` which is allowed.
In TypeScript files, getters must return a value (implicit return allowed).
In TypeScript files, a `return` statement must be preceded by an empty line unless it is first in its block.
In TypeScript files, code must not call alert, confirm or prompt.
In TypeScript files, `await` inside loops is allowed.
In TypeScript files, code must not use `console.*`; logging goes through LoggerService.
In TypeScript files, code must not contain `debugger` statements.
In TypeScript files, reassigning function parameters is allowed.
In TypeScript files, `++` and `--` operators are allowed.
In TypeScript files, `return await` is allowed.
In TypeScript files, identifiers with leading or trailing underscores are allowed.
In TypeScript files, the core `no-unused-vars` rule is disabled in favour of @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars.
In TypeScript files, code should not contain TODO/FIXME/XXX warning comments.
In package.json, an `exports` field is not required.
In package.json, a `files` field is not required.
In package.json, a `repository` field is not required.
In package.json, a `sideEffects` field is not required.
In package.json, a `type` field is not required.
In stories, playwright/vite/vitest config files and eslint.config.ts, default exports are allowed.
In **/*.d.ts declaration files, default exports are allowed.
In **/*.d.ts declaration files, type and class naming conventions are not enforced.
In **/*.d.ts declaration files, classes with only a constructor or static members are allowed.
In test files and __fixtures__, empty functions are allowed.
In test files and __fixtures__, referencing unbound methods (e.g. `expect(mock.method)`) is allowed.
In test files, Jest alias matchers (e.g. toBeCalled) must not be used; use canonical names (toHaveBeenCalled).
In test files, `expect` must not be called conditionally (inside if or catch).
In test files, tests must not be disabled with skip/xit/xdescribe.
In test files, tests and hooks must not use the `done` callback; use async/promises.
In test files, the file must not export anything.
In test files, focused tests (fit, fdescribe, .only) must not be committed.
In test files, sibling tests and describe blocks must not share the same title.
In test files, inline snapshots must not contain template interpolation.
In test files, Jasmine globals (spyOn, fail, pending, jasmine.*) must not be used.
In test files, modules must not be imported from `__mocks__` directories directly.
In test files, `expect` must only be called inside a test or hook, not at describe level.
In test files, `it.only`/`it.skip` must be used instead of the f/x prefixes (fit, xit, xdescribe).
In test files, array length assertions must use `toHaveLength()` instead of `expect(x.length).toBe(n)`.
In test files, `describe` callbacks must be synchronous functions without parameters.
In test files, `expect()` must be called with one argument and a matcher, and async matchers must be awaited.
In test files, promises containing `expect` must be returned or awaited.
In test files, describe/test titles must be non-empty strings without leading/trailing spaces or duplicated prefixes.
In **/__fixtures__/**, folder names need not be kebab-case.
In TypeScript files (not .d.ts), classes with only static members or empty bodies are forbidden unless decorated (e.g. NestJS @Module classes).

quote: api/           # Controllers and DTOs (transport layer only)
statement: In src/, controllers and DTOs must live under src/api/ (transport layer only).

quote: features/      # Business logic: services, repositories, entities, mappers
statement: In src/, business-logic services, repositories, entities and mappers must live under src/features/<feature>/.

quote: modules/       # Infrastructure modules (Redis, Prisma, Sentry, Metrics, etc.)
statement: In src/, infrastructure modules (Redis, Prisma, Sentry, Metrics, etc.) must live under src/modules/.

quote: common/        # Cross-cutting concerns: decorators, guards, interceptors, utils
statement: In src/, cross-cutting decorators, guards, interceptors and utils must live under src/common/.

In src/features/<feature>/, files must follow the anatomy: <feature>.service.ts, <feature>.repository.ts, <feature>.module.ts, constants/, entities/, mappers/, cache-queries/, types/, interfaces/ subfolders.
In src/api/<feature>/, the controller must be <feature>.controller.ts and DTOs must be split into dtos/requests/, dtos/responses/ and dtos/queries/.
In src/**, all file names must be kebab-case.

In src/**, file names must carry a role suffix (.service.ts, .controller.ts, .repository.ts, .module.ts, .entity.ts, .mapper.ts, .guard.ts, .interceptor.ts, .middleware.ts, .decorator.ts, .dto.ts, .enum.ts).
In src/**, unit test files must be co-located next to the file they test and named <name>.spec.ts.

quote: Base/abstract classes prefixed with `_base.` (e.g. `_base.error.ts`, `_base.client.ts`). The eslint filename-naming-convention rule is suppressed on these with a comment.
statement: In src/**, files holding base/abstract classes must be named `_base.<role>.ts` and suppress @check-file/filename-naming-convention with an eslint-disable comment.
In src/error-handler/errors/, error classes must be grouped into one `<domain>.errors.ts` file per domain.

quote: Use `type` over `interface` for shapes, with exceptions for NestJS-imposed interfaces.
statement: In src/**, shapes must be declared with `type`, not `interface`, except where NestJS imposes an interface.
In src/**, type-only imports must use `import type`.

quote: Alphabetical ordering of class members (properties and methods both, properties first).
statement: In src/** classes, members must be ordered alphabetically, with properties before methods.

quote: Explicit return types on all public methods.
statement: In src/** classes, all public methods must declare explicit return types.

quote: `readonly` on all injected services and private fields where mutation is not needed.
statement: In src/** classes, injected services and non-mutated private fields must be `readonly`.

quote: Private class fields using `#` syntax for truly private state (e.g. `#appName`).
statement: In src/** classes, truly private state must use ECMAScript `#` private fields (e.g. `#appName`).

quote: Enums use `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE` for keys, camelCase or lowercase string values.
statement: In src/** enums, keys must be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and string values camelCase or lowercase.

quote: Avoid `any`; use generics or `unknown` where needed.
statement: In src/**, code should not use `any`; use generics or `unknown` instead.

quote: Use discriminated unions and conditional spread (`...(condition && { key: value })`) over verbose if/else assignments.
statement: In src/**, optional object keys must be added with conditional spread (`...(cond && { key: value })`) rather than if/else assignments.

quote: Imports are grouped and ordered as follows (enforced by `eslint-plugin-perfectionist`, `recommended-natural`): 1. `import type` from packages 2. Value imports from Node built-ins and packages 3. `import type` from relative paths 4. Value imports from relative paths
statement: In TypeScript files, imports must be grouped as: package type imports, package/built-in value imports, relative type imports, relative value imports, blank line between groups, natural sort within.
In src/**/*.module.ts, the @Module decorator must declare controllers, imports, providers and exports explicitly.

quote: Infrastructure modules (`PrismaModule`, `RedisManagerModule`, etc.) are imported where needed rather than made global.
statement: In src/**/*.module.ts, infrastructure modules (PrismaModule, RedisManagerModule, etc.) must not be @Global; consuming modules import them explicitly.

quote: `ConfigModule` (`isGlobal: true`) and `LoggerModule` (`@Global()`) are the only global modules — configs are injected via `@Inject(config.KEY)`.
statement: In src/**, only ConfigModule and LoggerModule may be global; no other module may use @Global() or isGlobal.
Controllers must be placed in src/api/<feature>/.

quote: Thin: no business logic. Responsible only for transport (routing, guards, response mapping).
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, controllers must contain no business logic, only routing, guards and response mapping.

quote: Use `@Controller({ path, version })` for versioned routes.
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, versioned controllers must use `@Controller({ path, version })`.

quote: Response objects built with `plainToInstance(ResponseDto, result, { excludeExtraneousValues: true })`.
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, responses must be built with `plainToInstance(ResponseDto, result, { excludeExtraneousValues: true })`.

quote: Decorator order on controller methods: @ApiErrors(...) // Swagger error documentation first; @ApiOk(...) // or @ApiPaginated / @ApiEmpty; @Post() // HTTP method decorator; @UseGuards(AuthGuard) // Guards last
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, method decorators must be ordered @ApiErrors, then @ApiOk/@ApiPaginated/@ApiEmpty, then the HTTP verb, then @UseGuards last.
Business services must be placed in src/features/<feature>/.

quote: Contain all business logic including cache coordination.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, services must hold all business logic, including cache reads and invalidation.

quote: All dependencies injected via constructor with `private readonly`.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, all dependencies must be injected through constructor parameters declared `private readonly`.

quote: Explicit return types on all methods.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, all service methods must declare explicit return types.

quote: Throw domain errors (`BaseError` subclasses), never raw strings or generic `Error`.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, services must throw BaseError subclasses and must never throw strings or generic `Error`.

quote: Only place that interacts with Prisma directly.
statement: In src/**, only repositories (src/features/**/*.repository.ts) may call Prisma/PrismaService directly.
In src/features/**/*.repository.ts, multi-step reads and writes must use `this.prisma.$transaction([...])`.

quote: Map Prisma models to domain entities via the feature's `Mapper` object.
statement: In src/features/**/*.repository.ts, Prisma rows must be converted to domain entities through the feature's Mapper object (e.g. `TodoMapper.toEntity`).

quote: Do not throw domain errors — return `undefined` for not-found, let the service decide.
statement: In src/features/**/*.repository.ts, repositories must not throw domain errors; they return `undefined` for not-found.

quote: Plain classes, no NestJS or Prisma decorators.
statement: In src/features/**/entities/*.entity.ts, entities must be plain classes without NestJS or Prisma decorators.
In src/features/**/entities/*.entity.ts, the entity constructor must take `Partial<Entity>` and call `Object.assign(this, partial)`.
In src/features/**/entities/*.entity.ts, entity properties must be listed alphabetically.

quote: `const` objects with plain methods only (no classes, no instances).
statement: In src/features/**/mappers/*.mapper.ts, mappers must be exported `const` objects of plain methods, not classes.

quote: Single responsibility: map from Prisma model to domain entity.
statement: In src/features/**/mappers/*.mapper.ts, mappers must only map Prisma models to domain entities.
In src/**, Prisma-generated types must be imported with `import type`.
In src/api/**/dtos/requests/*.dto.ts, every field must be validated with class-validator decorators.
In request DTOs, every field must carry `@ApiProperty` or `@ApiPropertyOptional`.
In request DTOs, `@ApiProperty*` decorators must come before validation decorators on each field.

quote: Boolean query params: transform with `@Transform(({ value }) => value === 'true' || value === true)`.
statement: In query DTOs, boolean fields must use `@Transform(({ value }) => value === 'true' || value === true)`.

quote: Numeric query params: use `@Type(() => Number)` with `@IsInt()`.
statement: In query DTOs, numeric fields must use `@Type(() => Number)` together with `@IsInt()`.
In src/api/**/dtos/responses/*.dto.ts, every property must carry `@Expose()` from class-transformer.
In response DTOs, nested object or array properties must carry `@Type(() => NestedDto)`.
In response DTOs, every property must carry `@ApiProperty()`.
In response DTOs, properties must be listed alphabetically.
In query DTOs, every field must be marked `@IsOptional()`.
In src/error-handler/errors/**, every domain error class must extend `BaseError<TDetails>`.
In src/error-handler/errors/**, each error class must declare static `code`, `domain`, `message` and `status` properties.

quote: Constructor delegates to `super()` using the static properties.
statement: In src/error-handler/errors/**, error constructors must call `super()` with the class's static message, code, domain and status.
In src/error-handler/constants/error.codes.ts, `ErrorCodes` enum values must be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE strings.
In src/**, there must be a single global `@Catch()` exception filter (GlobalExceptionFilter); no other exception filters.

quote: Internal errors (infra/unknown) never expose details to clients.
statement: In the exception filter, infrastructure and unknown errors must never include internal details in the client response.

quote: Sentry capture only for 5xx when `SENTRY_ENABLED`; domain 4xx are never sent.
statement: In the exception filter, errors must be sent to Sentry only for 5xx when SENTRY_ENABLED; domain 4xx errors must never be captured.

quote: Each config defined with `registerAs('configKey', factory)` from `@nestjs/config`.
statement: In src/config/*.config.ts, each config must be defined with `registerAs('configKey', factory)` from @nestjs/config.

quote: Config validated at startup using a validator class with `class-validator` decorators.
statement: In src/config/*.config.ts, the factory must validate env with a class-validator validator class via `validateConfig(...)`.

quote: Config has a corresponding interface that the factory returns.
statement: In src/config/*.config.ts, each factory must return a typed config shape defined in src/config/interfaces/.
In src/**, configs must be injected with `@Inject(config.KEY)` and typed `ConfigType<typeof config>`.

quote: All cache operations are in `CacheStorage` (wraps Redis).
statement: In src/**, all cache operations must go through `CacheStorage`.

quote: Every method has a `try/catch` that logs a warning on failure — cache errors never propagate to callers.
statement: In src/modules/redis-manager/storages/cache.storage.ts, every CacheStorage method must catch errors, log a warning and not rethrow.

quote: Cache keys defined in a `const` object with one function per key type (e.g. `TodosCacheKeys`).
statement: In src/features/**/cache-queries/*.cache-queries.ts, cache keys must be defined as functions on a `*CacheKeys` const object.

quote: Key naming pattern: `<version>:resource:id`, `<version>:resource:userId:*` (for pattern invalidation). Bump the version constant when the shape of a cached value changes.
statement: In cache-queries files, keys must follow `<CACHE_VERSION>:resource:id` and be prefixed with a CACHE_VERSION constant that is bumped when the cached shape changes.

quote: `delByPattern` walks the keyspace with `SCAN` and `UNLINK`; never use `KEYS`.
statement: In src/** Redis code, the Redis `KEYS` command must never be used; pattern deletion uses SCAN and UNLINK.

quote: On create/update/delete: invalidate related keys via `del` or `delByPattern`.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, create/update/delete methods must invalidate related cache keys via `del` or `delByPattern`.

quote: On read: check cache first; on miss, fetch, then `set`.
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, cached reads must follow cache-aside: get from cache, on miss fetch from repository, then `set`.

quote: `LoggerService` wraps pino. All logging goes through it.
statement: In src/**, all logging must go through `LoggerService`, not console or raw pino.

quote: Log methods accept a structured `Message` object:
statement: In src/**, LoggerService methods must be called with a structured Message object (e.g. `{ ctx, msg, ... }`), not a bare string.

quote: `ctx` field always set to the calling class name (use `ClassName.name`).
statement: In src/** logging calls, the `ctx` field must always be the calling class name via `ClassName.name`.
In src/**/*.guard.ts and *.interceptor.ts, every guard and interceptor class must be decorated with `@Injectable()`.
In src/** guards and interceptors, classes must implement `CanActivate` or `NestInterceptor` respectively.

quote: Reusable and focused — one concern per guard/interceptor.
statement: In src/** guards and interceptors, each class must handle a single concern.

quote: Negative test cases first, positive test cases after, in separate `describe` blocks separated by a blank line.
statement: In spec files, negative cases must be in a first `describe('negative cases')` block and positive cases in a following `describe('positive cases')` block, separated by a blank line.

quote: Descriptive test names that explain the behavior, not the implementation.
statement: In spec files, test names must describe behaviour, not implementation.
In unit spec files, the unit under test must be built with `Test.createTestingModule` from @nestjs/testing.
In spec files, `jest.clearAllMocks()` must be called in `beforeEach`.

quote: Inject real implementations where practical; substitute external dependencies with mocks via `useValue`.
statement: In unit spec files, external dependencies must be substituted with mocks provided via `useValue` in the testing module.

quote: Shared mocks live in `src/mocks/` and are reused across spec files.
statement: Shared test mocks must live in src/mocks/ and be imported by spec files rather than redefined inline.

quote: Mock objects are plain objects with `jest.fn()` for each method — no class mocking or `jest.spyOn`.
statement: In spec files and src/mocks/, mocks must be plain objects with `jest.fn()` per method; class mocking and `jest.spyOn` must not be used.
In spec files, typed error assertions must use `await expect(...).rejects.toBeInstanceOf(ErrorClass)`.

quote: Use `rejects.toMatchObject({ details: { id: '...' } })` to assert error payload.
statement: In spec files, error payload assertions must use `rejects.toMatchObject({ details: ... })`.

quote: Prefer `toBe` for reference/primitive equality, `toEqual` for deep equality.
statement: In spec files, `toBe` should be used for primitive/reference equality and `toEqual` for deep equality.
In spec files, side effects must be asserted explicitly with `toHaveBeenCalledWith`.

quote: Add `// eslint-disable-next-line @check-file/filename-naming-convention` at the top of the file.
statement: In src/**/_base.*.ts files, line 1 must be `// eslint-disable-next-line @check-file/filename-naming-convention`.

quote: Used only for true inheritance hierarchies — prefer composition otherwise.
statement: In src/**, base classes must be used only for true inheritance hierarchies; otherwise compose.

quote: Keys in `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`. String values in `camelCase` or `lowercase` to match DB/API conventions.
statement: In src/**/*.enum.ts, enum keys must be SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE and string values camelCase or lowercase.

quote: Each enum in its own file or grouped by domain (e.g. `queries.enum.ts`).
statement: In src/**, enums must be declared in dedicated `*.enum.ts` files (one per enum or per domain).

quote: Grouped by concern in dedicated files (e.g. `url.constants.ts`).
statement: In src/**, constants must be placed in dedicated `*.constants.ts` files grouped by concern.
In src/**/*.constants.ts, constants must be named in SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE.

quote: New module exports only what consumers need
statement: In src/**/*.module.ts, a module's `exports` must list only providers that consuming modules use.

quote: New error codes added to `ErrorCodes` enum, categories to `ErrorCategory` enum
statement: In src/error-handler/**, new error codes must be added to the `ErrorCodes` enum and categories to `ErrorCategory`, not used as string literals.

quote: `CacheStorage` used for all Redis operations — no direct Redis access in services
statement: In src/features/**/*.service.ts, services must use `CacheStorage` and must not access Redis clients directly.

quote: Every log call includes `ctx: ClassName.name` and `msg`
statement: In src/**, every LoggerService call must include `ctx: ClassName.name` and `msg`.

quote: No sensitive data logged (auth tokens, passwords, cookies)
statement: In src/**, log calls must not include auth tokens, passwords or cookies.

quote: No test depends on execution order of other tests
statement: In test files, no test may depend on the execution order of other tests.

quote: Comments added only where the "why" is non-obvious
statement: In all source files, comments should only explain non-obvious reasoning.
A feature's domain errors must be placed in src/error-handler/errors/<feature>.errors.ts.
Create DTOs must be at src/api/<feature>/dtos/requests/create-<feature>.dto.ts and use class-validator plus @ApiProperty.
In src/api/<feature>/dtos/requests/update-<feature>.dto.ts, all fields must be optional.
Response DTOs must be at src/api/<feature>/dtos/responses/<feature>-response.dto.ts and use @Expose() and @ApiProperty.

quote: `src/features/<feature>/<feature>.repository.ts` — inject `PrismaService`, return entities via mapper, return `void` for not-found.
statement: In src/features/<feature>/<feature>.repository.ts, the repository must inject PrismaService, return entities via the mapper, and return void/undefined for not-found.

quote: `src/features/<feature>/<feature>.service.ts` — inject repository (and `CacheStorage` if caching applies), throw domain errors, coordinate cache invalidation.
statement: In src/features/<feature>/<feature>.service.ts, the service must inject the repository (and CacheStorage when caching), throw domain errors and coordinate cache invalidation.
A feature's cache key functions must be placed in src/features/<feature>/cache-queries/<feature>.cache-queries.ts.

quote: const CACHE_VERSION = 'v1'; // bump when the cached shape changes
statement: In cache-queries files, a `CACHE_VERSION` constant must prefix every key and be bumped when the cached value shape changes.
Every new feature module must be imported in src/app.module.ts.

quote: Unit tests: a co-located `*.spec.ts` next to the controller, service, repository, mapper and cache queries, with negative cases first
statement: Each feature's controller, service, repository, mapper and cache-queries file must have a co-located *.spec.ts with negative cases first.
End-to-end tests for a feature must be placed in test/<feature>.e2e-spec.ts.

quote: Exported from `PrismaModule`, which is not global: modules that need `PrismaService` import `PrismaModule`.
statement: In src/**/*.module.ts, any module whose providers inject PrismaService must import PrismaModule (which is not global).

quote: `RequestTrackingService` counts in-flight requests; it is a singleton provided by `RequestTrackingModule` (imported by `AppModule` for the middleware and by `ShutdownModule`), never redeclared elsewhere.
statement: In src/**/*.module.ts, `RequestTrackingService` must only be provided by RequestTrackingModule and never listed in another module's providers.

quote: `AuthGuard` is applied per-route with `@UseGuards(AuthGuard)`. Routes decorated with `@Public()` bypass it.
statement: In src/api/**/*.controller.ts, authenticated routes must apply `@UseGuards(AuthGuard)` per route; public routes are marked `@Public()`.

quote: **Rule:** code, comments, docs and the guide are written in English.
statement: In all source files, identifiers and comments must be written in English.

quote: Jest loads `globalSetup` and `globalTeardown` from a default export; everything else uses named exports.
statement: In all TypeScript files except test/setup/setup.global.ts and teardown.global.ts, modules must use named exports only.

quote: Only public methods should be tested. The internal implementation of a module is not the concern of a test
statement: In spec files, tests should exercise only public methods, not private internals.

quote: Every service test should include: positive cases - expected successful behavior; negative cases - validation failures and error scenarios
statement: In service spec files, tests should include both positive and negative cases.

quote: Endpoints that return collections should always support pagination.
statement: In src/api/** controllers, endpoints returning collections should accept pagination parameters and return paginated results.

quote: Never use the Redis `KEYS` command in production code: it scans the whole keyspace in a single blocking call and stalls all other clients.
statement: In src/**, Redis code must never call the `KEYS` command; use SCAN with UNLINK.

quote: `RequestTrackingService` must be a single instance: it is provided only by `RequestTrackingModule`
statement: In src/**/*.module.ts, `RequestTrackingService` must not be declared in any module's providers other than RequestTrackingModule.

quote: Users should never see raw database errors.
statement: In src/**, raw Prisma/database errors must never be returned to clients; they are mapped (mapPrismaError) first.

quote: A backend application should have a single global exception filter responsible for handling all unhandled errors.
statement: In src/**, unhandled errors should be handled by a single global exception filter.

quote: Additionally, unnecessary or unsafe fields should be removed during validation.
statement: In request validation, unknown or unsafe fields should be stripped (whitelisting DTOs).

quote: incoming requests (method, path and trace ID only, never the body)
statement: In request logging, incoming requests must be logged with method, path and trace ID only, never the request body (except at debug level).

quote: The `route` label is the route template (for example `/api/v1/todos/:id`), never the raw URL, so cardinality stays bounded.
statement: In metrics code, the `route` label must be the route template, never the raw URL.

quote: Using getOrThrow ensures that the application fails fast if a required configuration value is missing.
statement: When reading config from ConfigService, code should use `configService.getOrThrow(...)` rather than `get(...)`.
